questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Finding a place within EU, place with interesting history and location, interesting and relevant courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not happy with the university and the courses that I got - I was not able to choose any of the courses that I originally wanted.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy and if not, you can contact the staff and they are very happy to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation and an international office we could go to if we had any queries

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find accommodation, if you are willing to pay a lot of money for housing. I was only able to find one accommodation, which was extremely pricy, and it ended up being the same place that my host institution found for me. One semester students generally had fewer options.  I paid around 1400 euros per month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is extremely expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Most of it was online, but we also had to get our letter of arrival signed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could go to the international office for questions (on campus).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not at all, almost none of them were available. We had to register for our classes one week before arrival, which meant I didn't know my courses until one week before I left. I only got 2 out of 6 courses I wanted, and had to choose "random" courses to avoid timetable conflicts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be too afraid of timetable conflicts, if you have a few days of overlap, it will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not satisfied at all. The classes ran from second week of September till end of November. I had 6 different courses of 5 credits each (i wasn't really able to find 10 credit courses) which meant that we weren't really able to deep dive into any material. This was supported by the fact that 5/6 of my courses had lectures that only lasted 50 min pr class. Most of the classes had deadlines piled up at the same time in end of November, which meant a huge workload in that period, instead of spreading it out over a longer period.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'm a BA I took one MA and I did not experience any difference in the level - I found some of my freshman courses more difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I sometimes think the Blok system makes it hard to really do a deep dive into the material that you are working with, and find that a bit frustrating some times. This was even worse, 5 credit courses and 6 different courses at the same time in the span of 3 months does not work at all. I only had one class with exercises all other classes consisted only of lectures that lasted no longer than 50 minutes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GG1014 - Human geographies 
GG2046 - Atmosphere, weather and climate 
GG2044 - People, places and politics 
MS1002 - Calculus 
GS4004 - Advanced igneous processes 
GL6024 - Applied Geophysics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Applied Geophysics (in only runs for 2 weeks though) and People, Places and Politics (interesting  if you want to learn something about the place you are staying).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs and societies linked to the university almost everything you can think of. Also a lot of activities for international students to go sightseeing for instance.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds of sports and societies

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join any club or society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips organised for the the international students

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Irish people are very sweet and welcoming - although you don't really have that much to do with them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were very proud of their traditions and very good at keeping them alive- Live music at pubs, folklore etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go there for the experience and not the courses 
Be prepared to pay a lot of money 
Cork and Ireland is an amazing place

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The place I stayed at (Lee Point) was in the dead center - this meant that there was constant music and noise from pubs and clubs, so be prepared for this. The swap shop, which is organized by UCC has a lot of stuff that you can get. They have tons of pillows and duvets available, so dont spend money on a new one, just get one from them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture and they place, and my roomies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses, I did not really enjoy them that much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
